Asian restaurants in the west are usually zero atmosphere holes in the wall in strip malls, even when the food's fantastic. This is unlike most other restaurants where zero-atmosphere strip malls are usually the domain of low end fast food restaurants. Why is this?
Why do Asian restsurants (in the West) usually have no atmosphere?

• Margins in the restaurant business are terrible

  • These restaurants are frequently family-run, with minimal capital

  • The food is fantastic but the ingredients are usually cheap as hell, so it's really still a low-end restaurant

  • When you get away from the strip malls you can usually find at least some semblance of decor - lacquer paintings, silver bowls, etc.
Because most of the restaurants here in Asia are basically the same way. I could post a million pictures from my neighborhood alone to show the correlation.
